title: Durably reverse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

concept.text: The proposed innovation is durable reversal of established heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF): restoring the heart’s filling physiology and the patient’s capacity for daily activity, with lasting improvement in cardiac function and clinical outcomes. Preserved ejection fraction alone would not demonstrate recovery; the target is the underlying failure of cardiovascular function despite preservation of that particular measure. This describes a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The working premise in the research is that HFpEF encompasses different combinations of myocardial, vascular, metabolic and other systemic contributors. Accordingly, the innovation could be a matched set of treatments for different patients rather than a single drug or molecular intervention. The supplied scientific material does not verify that mechanistic account or establish the absence of a universally effective intervention, so these remain premises to substantiate rather than demonstrated conclusions of this record.

significance.text: Conditional assessment: reliably restoring filling physiology, exercise capacity and durable cardiac function across major forms of HFpEF would change the therapeutic objective from managing an ongoing syndrome to reversing established disease. Direct benefits would include better daily function and fewer heart-failure events if both were demonstrated. The revolutionary claim depends on physiological recovery and sustained patient benefit together; improvement in an event endpoint alone would not establish the full capability.

Conditional downstream possibilities include less recurrent care and a reduced long-term burden of illness for patients who achieve sustained recovery. The breadth of that impact would depend on response rates, which patient groups benefit, treatment safety and the persistence of benefit. Describing HFpEF as a condition that can often be reversed would require evidence of both substantial population coverage and sufficiently frequent successful reversal. Neither follows automatically from success in a selected subgroup.

Interpretive limit: durable recovery need not require treatment withdrawal in every circumstance. Continued therapy might maintain a restored state, whereas other interventions might produce lasting benefit after a finite course. These possibilities should be described separately. Symptom relief during treatment, fewer clinical events and restoration of normal physiology are distinct achievements, even when all are valuable.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is a reproducible way to restore filling physiology and functional capacity in established HFpEF, with durable clinical benefit across prospectively defined major patient groups. Whether that capability remains unachieved throughout the field cannot be determined from the supplied evidence. The development challenge is nevertheless clear: demonstrate reversal of the disease process rather than infer it from improved symptoms or reduced events.

Scientific and engineering barriers identified by the concept’s working model include determining which contributors drive disease in a particular patient, identifying which abnormalities remain reversible, and selecting or combining interventions that address those contributors. If myocardial, vascular and systemic mechanisms differ among patients, successful translation would require reliable patient classification and treatment matching. The supplied material does not establish a single molecular cause or show that one mechanism explains all major forms.

Proposed development requirements also include measurements that connect physiological recovery to meaningful daily function, and study designs that distinguish durable change from benefit dependent on continuing therapy. Major subgroups, the magnitude of restoration and the duration of follow-up need explicit definitions. These are unresolved design requirements, not published consensus criteria supplied with this record.

current_state.text: The research attributes a treatment advance to a pooled analysis of randomized semaglutide trials, identified as a Lancet publication dated 30 August 2024, titled “Semaglutide versus placebo in patients with heart failure and mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction,” with DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01643-X. It reports fewer clinical heart-failure events in selected populations described as having metabolic or other comorbidities. These bibliographic details, trial characteristics, population descriptions and findings are supplied attributions; the review could not verify them from the retained source.

The retained copy of the cited PubMed page exposes only a cookie-access notice, with no article identity, abstract or scientific results. Consequently, the earlier statement that the assessment relied on the abstract is not supported. Although the source index records a saved, untruncated extraction, the review establishes that the intended scientific document was unavailable in that extraction. This access limitation leaves the reported finding unverified here; it does not show that the publication or result is false.

If the reported pooled result is confirmed, fewer clinical heart-failure events would support a treatment advance in the studied populations. It would not by itself establish restored normal filling physiology, persistence after treatment withdrawal, effectiveness across major HFpEF forms or a general cure. The reported inclusion of mildly reduced as well as preserved ejection fraction also makes the precise population and subgroup results relevant to interpreting the evidence specifically for HFpEF.

The supplied review contains no usable freshness search establishing the field’s status through 1 November 2026. The retained page was retrieved on 11 November 2026, but that retrieval provides no newer scientific findings. This record therefore cannot substantiate either a sweeping historical description of HFpEF as largely untreatable or a definitive present-day claim that durable reversal has been achieved or remains unachieved. No inspectable effect sizes, follow-up durations or quantitative physiological results were supplied.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: controlled studies in patients with established HFpEF should show sustained normalization or substantial restoration of filling physiology, accompanied by improved exercise capacity or daily function and fewer heart-failure events. Physiological, functional and clinical outcomes should be assessed together so that success on one measure does not substitute for evidence of the others. These are proposed requirements for this innovation, not established standards documented in the supplied sources.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained filling restoration with functional gains and fewer heart-failure events

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility requirements: studies should prospectively define major HFpEF subgroups, specify how treatments are matched to patients, and report response rates and nonresponse within each group. Independent replication across relevant settings would strengthen the case that the result extends beyond one selected population or study. A finite program could establish demonstrated breadth across those groups, not literal effectiveness for every possible patient or disease mechanism.
completion_criteria.label: Report response and nonresponse across prospectively defined HFpEF subgroups

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability requirements: investigators should define meaningful restoration thresholds and follow-up periods before evaluating success, and distinguish sustained recovery during continued treatment from benefit persisting after treatment ends. Where withdrawal is clinically appropriate, follow-up after treatment could test persistence; where maintenance therapy is necessary, that dependence should be explicit. The supplied material does not justify a particular numerical threshold or duration.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified durability criteria distinguish recovery during and after treatment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: convincing evidence should identify residual impairment, recurrence, adverse effects, treatment burden and patient groups for whom reversal is incomplete or absent. A claim of broad clinical usefulness would also require a feasible way to identify eligible patients and deliver the necessary treatment or combination. The final claim should match the demonstrated population, magnitude of recovery and duration of benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Report reversal limits and feasibility of patient selection and treatment

related_concepts.text: Conceptual comparison with the supplied roster: CAR-01, “Regenerate a severely damaged adult human heart,” concerns rebuilding damaged myocardium, whereas CAR-08 concerns restoring filling physiology and function in HFpEF. Regeneration could be relevant to some proposed mechanisms without being required for every route to HFpEF reversal. CAR-03, “A durable, broadly affordable total artificial heart,” CAR-04, “A dependable supply of transplantable animal hearts,” and CAR-07, “Produce a transplantable, fully engineered living human heart,” pursue replacement strategies. Their success would not itself establish reversal of disease in the patient’s existing heart.

Conceptual comparison: CAR-02, “Reliably reverse advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree,” and CAR-12, “Detect actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event,” address arterial disease and coronary risk. They overlap with the vascular dimension of the HFpEF working model, but plaque reversal or risk detection would not establish recovery of HFpEF physiology. CAR-10, “Reverse established calcific aortic stenosis without valve replacement,” and CAR-11, “Reverse pulmonary arterial hypertension and its cardiovascular consequences,” concern distinct valve and pulmonary vascular targets. Any contribution to HFpEF recovery would need direct demonstration rather than being assumed from success against those targets.

Conceptual comparison: CAR-05, “Correct inherited heart disease directly and durably in the beating heart,” targets inherited causes, while CAR-08 permits different acquired or systemic contributors and different treatments. CAR-09, “A durable, non-ablative cure for atrial fibrillation,” targets a rhythm disorder; rhythm correction and HFpEF reversal are separate endpoints. CAR-06, “Make most preventable sudden cardiac deaths predictable and preventable,” focuses on prediction and prevention of fatal events, which does not establish restored filling physiology or daily function.

Conceptual comparison: CAR-13, “Broadly prevent cardiac injury from cancer treatment without weakening cancer control,” addresses prevention of treatment-related injury, whereas CAR-08 addresses reversal of established HFpEF. Preventing injury could reduce later disease burden without demonstrating reversal once disease exists. These comparisons preserve the roster entries as distinct innovations; they do not establish shared mechanisms or proven therapeutic dependencies.

unresolved_issues: An inspectable version of the cited publication is needed to verify its identity, bibliographic details, randomized design, pooled populations, endpoints and reported results.
The magnitude of event reduction, follow-up duration, HFpEF-specific findings and any physiological or post-treatment persistence measurements remain unavailable in the supplied evidence.
The supplied material does not establish the mechanistic breadth of HFpEF, the absence of a universally effective intervention or the field’s status through 1 November 2026.
Major HFpEF subgroups, meaningful restoration thresholds, follow-up duration and circumstances in which treatment withdrawal is appropriate remain undefined.
The response rates, population coverage, safety and practical delivery requirements needed to support broad durable reversal remain to be demonstrated.

brief.title: Lasting recovery from heart failure with filling problems
possible: People could regain daily activity and lasting heart function after developing heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. This means heart failure despite a preserved share of blood pumped out with each beat. Recovery would restore how the heart fills with blood and patients’ ability to function.
why: For patients, sustained recovery would mean better daily function, fewer episodes of worsening heart failure and less recurrent care. Treatment would aim to reverse established disease rather than manage an ongoing illness.

sources.who: Mikhail Kosiborod and collaborating trial investigators
sources.showed: A pooled analysis of randomized trials found that semaglutide reduced worsening heart failure in selected patients. It did not show a significant reduction in cardiovascular death alone.
sources.quote: In patients with HFpEF, semaglutide reduced the risk of the combined endpoint of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure events, and worsening heart failure events alone, whereas its effect on cardiovascular death alone was not significant.
sources.cited_for: Semaglutide can reduce clinical episodes of worsening heart failure.
sources.not_established: Fewer episodes do not establish restored filling, lasting recovery after treatment ends or effectiveness across major patient groups.

sources.showed: In a small randomized trial involving patients with obesity, semaglutide lowered heart filling pressures. Over half of treated patients reached normal pressures at rest and during exercise.
sources.quote: semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission
sources.cited_for: Treatment can restore normal filling pressures in some patients with obesity.
sources.not_established: This trial does not establish lasting recovery after treatment ends or broad recovery across different forms of heart failure.

sources.who: Milton Packer and the SUMMIT Trial Study Group
sources.showed: In patients with obesity, tirzepatide reduced worsening heart failure and improved health status. Side effects caused some patients to stop treatment.
sources.quote:
Treatment with tirzepatide led to a lower risk of a composite of death from cardiovas-
cular causes or worsening heart failure than placebo and improved health status in 
patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity.
sources.cited_for: Tirzepatide provides clinical benefits in patients with obesity.
sources.not_established: The trial does not establish restored filling physiology or recovery that persists after treatment ends.

sources.showed: Combined endurance and strength training improved exercise capacity and symptom severity. The trial missed its main combined outcome and found no significant improvement in its measure of heart filling.
sources.quote:
Time 
to all-cause death or cardiovascular hospitalization was also not sig-
nificantly different between groups
sources.cited_for: Exercise training can improve function without demonstrating overall disease reversal.
sources.not_established: Better exercise capacity did not establish restored filling or fewer hospitalizations.

shown: Barry Borlaug and colleagues have demonstrated normal heart filling pressures during semaglutide treatment in some patients with obesity. Alongside trials showing better health status and fewer episodes of worsening heart failure, this establishes progress toward recovery.
missing: Controlled studies still need to demonstrate restored filling, better daily function and fewer heart-failure events together, with sustained benefit.
Recovery needs to be reproduced across patient groups defined before studies begin, with clear rates of success and nonresponse.
Studies need to distinguish recovery maintained by continued treatment from recovery that persists after treatment ends.
Broad clinical use needs practical patient selection and treatment delivery, with clear evidence on recurrence, remaining impairment and harms.

milestones.label: Sustained filling recovery, better function and fewer heart-failure events
milestones.explanation: Controlled studies would have to show sustained restoration of heart filling alongside better activity and fewer heart-failure events. Together, these would demonstrate recovery in both heart function and patients’ lives.

milestones.label: Reproducible recovery across patient groups defined in advance
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to define patient groups and treatment matching in advance, report response and nonresponse, and reproduce results independently. This would establish how broadly recovery applies.

milestones.label: Lasting recovery distinguished during and after treatment
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to set recovery thresholds and follow-up periods in advance, distinguishing continued treatment from persistence after it ends. This would clarify what lasting recovery means.

milestones.label: Clear recovery limits and practical treatment delivery
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to report remaining impairment, recurrence, harms, treatment burden and who does not recover, alongside feasible patient selection and delivery. This would establish the practical reach of treatment.

uncertain: The degree of restoration and length of follow-up needed to count as durable recovery remain undefined.
It remains unclear which patient groups need different treatments and how reliably treatment can be matched to each.
When treatment can safely end, and when continued therapy is necessary to maintain recovery, remain open questions.

page.title: Recovery from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
page.definition: A treatment produces sustained normalization of cardiac structure, filling function, biomarkers and symptoms in established heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Ejection fraction is the proportion of left-ventricular blood ejected per beat; its preservation alone does not establish recovery.

goal.need: In its 2020 assessment, the NHLBI working group estimated that HFpEF accounted for nearly half of heart failure cases. Its estimates of US prevalence and survival after hospitalization quantify the population affected and the risk faced by patients with established disease.

figures.caption: HFpEF burden summarized by the NHLBI working group in 2020
rows: Survival five years after HF hospitalization
figures.note: These are estimates summarized in the 2020 report, rather than measurements of the population in 2026.

statements.body: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute HFpEF Working Group
statements.quote: Perform early-phase proof-of-concept clinical trials as part of a specific HFpEF clinical research network.
statements.context: A recommendation in the working group's published research priorities.

statements.body: European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial Function
statements.quote: major steps in patient management and therapeutic development are badly needed.
statements.context: The HFpEF position paper was published online on 16 November 2017.

completion.title: Patients with HFpEF sustain normal cardiac structure, function, biomarkers and freedom from symptoms.
completion.criterion: Patients with established HFpEF achieve sustained normalization of cardiac structure, function, biomarkers and symptoms over extended follow-up, meeting the joint societies' general definition of HF recovery. This definition specifies no minimum follow-up duration, required response fraction or HFpEF-specific physiological cutoffs. Preserved ejection fraction alone does not meet it.
completion.set_by: AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Task Force, Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure, section on HF trajectories. This is a general HF recovery definition applied here to HFpEF.
completion.threshold_quote: sustained normalization of cardiac structure, function, biomarkers, and symptoms over extended follow-up.
completion.basis: The joint societies distinguish recovery from remission and from improvement in ejection fraction. Their definition matches reversal of the syndrome across clinical and cardiac domains. It supplies a qualitative completion criterion, rather than an HFpEF-specific validated trial endpoint; the duration represented by extended follow-up remains unspecified.

milestones.title: An HFpEF animal model preserves ejection fraction and develops exercise intolerance.
milestones.criterion: An animal model reproduces HFpEF with documented exercise intolerance, preserved ejection fraction and cardiac filling abnormalities. The ESC position paper rejects models lacking effort intolerance. Published on 10 April 2019, a high-fat-diet plus L-NAME mouse study demonstrated preserved ejection fraction, pulmonary congestion and reduced running distance after 15 weeks: 15 mice per group for ejection fraction and lung measurements, eight per group for exercise. The demonstrated model represents obesity-associated HFpEF.
milestones.set_by: European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial Function, position paper on translational HFpEF research.
milestones.threshold_quote: no model should be presented as HFpEF without clear documentation of effort intolerance.

milestones.title: Patients with HFpEF increase peak oxygen uptake by at least 15% during 12 months.
milestones.criterion: Increase peak oxygen uptake, the maximum oxygen consumption during exercise, by ≥15% from baseline, using Ex-DHF's last available assessment during 12-month follow-up. Published on 2 January 2025, Ex-DHF randomized 322 patients, 161 per group; 53 exercise-training and 24 usual-care patients entered this improvement category. The mean between-group difference was 1.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI 0.4–2.1). The primary composite endpoint was not met (P=0.17), and E/e′, an ultrasound estimate of filling pressure, did not improve significantly. Obesity-specific response counts were not provided.
milestones.set_by: Ex-DHF investigators, registered study ISRCTN86879094. The ≥15% component threshold is stated in Table 2 of the published report.

milestones.title: A treatment reduces the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening HF in HFpEF at α=0.04.
milestones.criterion: Show fewer cardiovascular deaths or adjudicated worsening-HF events versus placebo at α=0.04. Worsening HF requires increased symptoms leading to hospitalization, urgent intravenous treatment or increased oral diuretics. SUMMIT followed 731 patients with LVEF ≥50% and body mass index ≥30 kg/m² for ≥52 weeks. At median 104 weeks, events were 36/364 versus 56/367 (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41–0.95; P=0.026; published on 16 November 2024). A separate post-hoc semaglutide pool (n=3,743; published on 30 August 2024) found composite HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.53–0.89), including mildly reduced EF.
milestones.set_by: SUMMIT steering committee and sponsor, amended protocol and statistical analysis plan reported in the primary publication. This endpoint was specified for HFpEF with obesity.
milestones.threshold_quote: assessed in a time-to-first-event analysis (with an alpha allocation of 0.04)

milestones.title: Patients with HFpEF reach filling pressures <15 mmHg at rest and <25 mmHg at 20 W after 52 weeks.
milestones.criterion: At 52 weeks, pulmonary artery wedge pressure, an invasive measure of left-heart filling pressure, is <15 mmHg at rest and <25 mmHg during the protocol's 20-W exercise assessment. Published on 8 November 2026, CAMEO-SEMA randomized 81 patients with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide or placebo; hemodynamic remission occurred in 53.7% versus 7.4% (odds ratio 14.1, 95% CI 3.0–134.6; P<0.001). Assessment occurred during treatment. This result does not establish remission without obesity or persistence after treatment withdrawal.
milestones.set_by: Mayo Clinic CAMEO-SEMA investigators, NCT05371496, protocol and statistical analysis plan, hemodynamic remission analysis. The published threshold was tested in HFpEF with obesity.
milestones.threshold_quote: the binomial indicator will be defined as PAWP <15 mmHg at rest and PAWP <25 mmHg during exercise

milestones.title: HFpEF symptoms, signs and previously present structural and functional heart disease resolve.
milestones.criterion: In previously symptomatic HFpEF, resolve HF symptoms and signs together with the previously present structural and functional heart disease, meeting the 2021 universal definition's remission criterion. This precedes demonstration of sustained normalization, including biomarkers, required for recovery. The CAMEO-SEMA filling-pressure endpoint alone does not establish this combined state.
milestones.set_by: Heart Failure Society of America, Heart Failure Association of the ESC and Japanese Heart Failure Society, 2021 Universal Definition and Classification of Heart Failure. This remission criterion concerns HF generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: resolution of symptoms and signs of HF along with resolution of previously present structural and functional heart disease

not_found: No HFpEF-specific minimum duration, responder fraction or treatment-withdrawal requirement for full recovery was found in the society definitions, HFpEF guidance or trial protocols searched.
No controlled demonstration satisfying every domain of full recovery was located for either obesity phenotype.
Obesity-stratified Ex-DHF results for its ≥15% oxygen-uptake response threshold were not located.
